packageRules.description: Crates: Cargo.lock within the caret ranges, or a range in Cargo.toml when a release falls outside it, both cargo roots, one pull request, with major updates in a pull request of their own beside it (separateMajorMinor). One of the two groups that skip the held default: it opens without a dashboard click, once a release is seven days old, and a person merges it. Lock-file maintenance stays held by its own rule below, and a vulnerability fix does not wait for the seven days.

The upstream parser is never updated here. An upstream bump is a release of this repository (decisions 0010 and 0011), done through docs/how-to/bump-upstream.md, and just version-check fails a bare bump by design. The rule matches the manager rather than a file, so it covers both cargo roots; an exact requirement holds lock-file maintenance at the pin. This rule stays off for a vulnerability-fix pull request too: those rules never set enabled.

Remote actions, SHA and version comment together, one pull request, with major updates in a pull request of their own beside it (separateMajorMinor). The other group that skips the held default: it opens without a dashboard click, once a release is seven days old, and a person merges it. A vulnerability fix does not wait for the seven days.

The toolchain: channel in rust-toolchain.toml and rust-version in both manifests, one pull request. rust-release-channel versioning keeps the precision of the value it replaces, so rust-version stays major.minor. Held for dashboard approval, because a toolchain moves the clippy lint set; a vulnerability-fix pull request skips that approval.

The flake's inputs in flake.lock (nixpkgs, rust-overlay, crane): one pull request, because nixpkgs moves every tool the dev shell holds at once (decision 0018). Held for dashboard approval; a vulnerability-fix pull request skips that approval. The nix manager is beta; if the hosted app cannot relock flake.lock, the pull request fails lock-check and the routine is just lock-upgrade by hand (docs/how-to/maintain-dependencies.md).

uv in the release job's setup-uv version, read from uv's own GitHub releases. The release workflow never used the dev shell, so its pin moves on its own. Held for dashboard approval; a vulnerability-fix pull request skips that approval.
maturin in every maturin-version input of the release workflow, read from PyPI. Held for dashboard approval; a vulnerability-fix pull request skips that approval.
python-version inputs of setup-python are manual: 3.11 is the abi3 floor of decision 0012 and 3.14t is the free-threaded build the release matrix smokes, so neither is a version to bump.
The github-actions manager would also read setup-uv's version and maturin-action's maturin-version; the regex managers below own both, so each pin has one watcher.

The maturin range in build-system.requires. The dev shell's maturin is what builds locally and in just check, and the release workflow sets maturin-version, so neither reads this range; it is what a user's installer honours when it builds the sdist. PyPI itself builds nothing. The range is kept rather than pinned, and Renovate proposes widening or replacing it on a maturin 2.0. Held for dashboard approval; a vulnerability-fix pull request skips that approval.

Lock-file maintenance rewrites both Cargo lockfiles and, through the nix manager, flake.lock: every tool the dev shell holds moves with it. Held for dashboard approval; a vulnerability-fix pull request skips that approval.

twine in the release workflow's check of every job's dist/: first exercised by the release rehearsal, because the workflow does not run on pull requests. Held for dashboard approval; a vulnerability-fix pull request skips that approval.

customManagers.description: rust-version in the workspace and fuzz manifests, grouped with the native rust-toolchain manager's channel.

The release job's setup-uv version, from uv's GitHub releases. The pattern is bound to the setup-uv step, so another action's version input is not read; version must stay the step's first input, or this stops matching.
twine in the release workflow's TWINE_CHECK script.
